justification.statement: 2 < sqrt(5) < 3, and the sign of a + b sqrt(5) is decided by exact comparison of rationals
justification.text: Since 4 < 5 < 9, 2 < √5 < 3. A number a + b√5 with a and b of the same sign has that sign; with opposite signs its sign is that of the larger of a² and 5b², taken with its own term's sign.

reason.statement: 2 < sqrt(5) < 3, and the sign of a + b sqrt(5) is decided by exact comparison of rationals
reason.idea: An exact number with a square root of 5 is compared with zero by squaring, never by a decimal approximation, so a sign is never wrong by rounding.

failure.outcome: weaker conclusion: with a decimal approximation of √5 the sign of a number very close to 0 can come out wrong; only exact arithmetic gives the sign

by_hand.not_meant: A sign says nothing about which pose or piece a number belongs to.
